sentences.text: He has been sentenced to varying terms of imprisonment for the aforesaid offences.
The sentences have been directed to run concurrently.
The maximum period of imprisonment he will have to undergo is ten years.
2. The learned counsel for the applicant/A1 submitted that the evidence on record is insufficient to establish the offence of rape alleged against the applicant/A1.
Though in the FIS there is an allegation of rape, in the testimony of PW2, she has no such case.
Crl.M.Appl. No.1 of 2024 in Crl.
Appeal No.782 of 2024 and The applicant/A1 is her neighbour, but there is no reference to the name of the applicant/A1 in the history narrated to the doctor.
In the FIR also, the name of the applicant/A1 is not referred to.
On the other hand, the accused is stated to be unknown.
It is also pointed out that PW2 is a hearing and speech disabled person.
She was examined in the court with the help of an interpreter.
But a reading of the impugned judgment would show that the interpreter was also unable to decipher the answers given by PW2.
Hence based on the testimony of such a witness, it would be quite unsafe to find the applicant/A1 guilty of the offences alleged against him.

3. The application is opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor who submitted that this is a case of forcible rape committed by the applicant/A1 resulting in serious injuries to the private parts of the victim.
It was taking advantage of the disability of PW2, the applicant/A1 had committed rape.
Hence there is no infirmity in the impugned judgment and therefore no special circumstances are made out to suspend the sentence.
Crl.M.Appl. No.1 of 2024 in Crl. Appeal No.782 of 2024 and 4. I was taken through the FIS as well as the testimony of PW2, the victim in this case.
It is true that the word 'rape' has not been used by PW2 while she was examined in the box.
However, an entire reading of the testimony of PW2 would certainly make out a case that she was undressed and sexually abused by the applicant/A1.
PW2 is seen to have been examined without much delay by the doctor.
On examination, the doctor has reported an injury on the vaginal wall.
According to PW10-the doctor, there was a small abrasion over the posterior fourchette and a tear having a length of around 6 cm on the right lateral vaginal wall.
There was bleeding from the injuries noted.
The injuries noted were severe and hence the witness had to be given anesthesia for carrying out the suturing.

There was considerable loss of blood and hence 500 ml of blood was given to PW2.
5.

The argument of the learned counsel for the appellant that PW2 must have bled as she was menstruating at the relevant time, cannot be accepted because the doctor would certainly know Crl.M.Appl. No.1 of 2024 in Crl. Appeal No.782 of 2024 and whether it was menstrual bleeding or bleeding from the injury that was caused to her private parts.

From the injuries seen on the private parts of PW2, this appears to be a case where considerable force had been used during the sexual abuse and therefore I find that this is not a fit case in which sentence needs to be suspended.
In the result, this application is dismissed.
Post on 02/12/2025 for final hearing.

Sd/-
C.S.SUDHA JUDGE ami/ 10-04-2025 /True Copy/
